props.title: The Key to Rebecca
props.initialSlug: The truth is the deadliest weapon.

sections.content: **The Key to Rebecca (1985)** (1985) stands as a taut World War II espionage thriller adapted from Ken Follett's bestselling novel. Set against the backdrop of 1942 Cairo, the film follows Nazi spy Johannes Eppler (played by Cliff Robertson) as he uses a copy of Daphne du Maurier's **Rebecca** (1940) as a code book to transmit classified information to Rommel's Afrika Korps. The film builds on the rich tradition of WWII spy thrillers like **The Eye of the Needle** (1981) and **Night of the Generals** (1967), combining historical authenticity with suspenseful cat-and-mouse gameplay.

sections.content: The film's director, David Hemmings, brings his experience from **Raiders of the Lost Ark** (1981) to create authentic period atmosphere in the North African theater. Like **Casablanca** (1942) and **Five Graves to Cairo** (1943), the film captures the intrigue and tension of wartime espionage in exotic locales. David Soul delivers a compelling performance as British Intelligence officer Major William Vandam, engaged in a deadly game of wits with Robertson's spy. SUBHEAD: Espionage and Code Breaking in Cinema

**The Key to Rebecca** (1985) fits into a broader tradition of code-breaking war films like Enigma (2001) and **The Imitation Game** (2014). Its use of literature as an encryption device recalls similar plot devices in Charlotte Gray (2001) and **Windtalkers** (2002). The film effectively combines elements of both military intelligence procedurals and personal drama, as Vandam's pursuit becomes increasingly desperate with Rommel's forces threatening to take Cairo.
